advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Canonicalise caused_by_fan_in target_ids (via resolve_ticket_id / prefix index) before joining to ticket dirs, or assert the join rate so an unmatched target is visible rather than read as 0.
evidence: all_work.py: `ticket["caused_by"] = int(fan_in.get(ticket_id, 0))` keyed on full ticket dir name
build_report: `{str(k): int(v) for k, v in (caused_by_fan_in(str(repo_root)) or {}).items()}`
src/rebar/metrics/bug_trends.py:283 docstring: 'Targets are counted verbatim (they need not resolve to existing tickets).'
src/rebar/metrics/bug_trends.py:213 `target = edge["target_id"]` — key is the raw stored target, not a canonicalised ticket id

ABSENCE: no resolve_ticket_id / prefix normalisation is applied to fan_in keys before the .get() join, so a target_id that is not the exact directory name is invisible (reads 0) and indistinguishable from a genuine 'never named as a cause'
advisory.finding: caused_by fan-in is joined by exact full-ticket-id match, but caused_by_fan_in() keys are raw edge target_id strings that the metric explicitly documents 'need not resolve to existing tickets' / are 'counted verbatim'. Any target recorded in a short/non-canonical form silently reads 0, under-counting the caused_by signal with no error.
scenarios: A bug whose caused_by target_id was recorded as a 4-quad short prefix or a jira-key alias while the culprit's ticket directory is the full id — the fan-in count for that culprit ticket silently becomes 0.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether a rename is one file or two for the surface metric, and either dedupe rename pairs or document the double-count as intentional in build_report's methodology.
evidence: all_work.py `_diff_paths` docstring: 'renames count both sides'
`if target[:2] in ("a/", "b/"): target = target[2:]` then `paths.add(target)` — for a rename the old and new names differ, so both land in the set
files_touched/files_union are computed from len(paths) and drive the report's central files-surface bands
advisory.finding: _diff_paths counts a renamed file's a/ (old) and b/ (new) header paths as two distinct entries, inflating files_touched and files_union for renames — the file-surface variable the ADR promotes to an advisory.
scenarios: A change that renames N files with no other edits reports 2N files touched, biasing the files-touched distribution and correlations upward for rename-heavy commits.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider all ticket_refs (not just refs[0]) when resolving a commit to a single ticket, and document the tie-break, so an ambiguous first ref does not discard an otherwise resolvable commit.
evidence: `candidates = set(index.get(refs[0], [])) if refs else set()` — only refs[0] is consulted
`if len(candidates) != 1: unresolved += 1; continue` — an ambiguous first ref discards the commit even if a later ref were unambiguous
advisory.finding: group_by_ticket attributes each commit solely by its first ticket ref (refs[0]); a commit carrying multiple rebar-ticket refs whose intended ticket is not listed first is folded into the wrong ticket, and if refs[0] is an ambiguous 4-quad fragment resolving to >1 id the whole commit is dropped as unresolved.
scenarios: A commit trailer lists two rebar-ticket refs (e.g. an epic and its task) with the task second; the commit's shape is credited to the epic or dropped.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a unit test for group_by_ticket/ticket_ids covering a Jira-bridged directory (jira-reb-596) that must be counted and an ambiguous 4-char prefix that must fall to `unresolved`.
evidence: search_files for 'group_by_ticket' returns only definition+call sites in scripts/_backtest/all_work.py, no tests/ hit — ABSENCE of any regression test
scripts/_backtest/all_work.py:159 `def group_by_ticket(rows, full_ids) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[str, Any]], int]:` folds by first ref and counts unresolved when `len(candidates) != 1`

scripts/_backtest/all_work.py ticket_ids docstring: 'filtering to the four-quad shape silently drops them from the corpus' — the corrected behavior the commit message calls out (jira-reb-596/jira-reb-687)

Named violating inputs with no test: (a) a Jira-bridged id 'jira-reb-596' as a directory + a commit trailer resolving to it must be COUNTED (the corrected behavior); (b) a bare 4-char ref '0880' that _prefix_index maps to two full ids must land in `unresolved`, not be silently attributed to one ticket
advisory.finding: The new corpus-folding logic group_by_ticket / _prefix_index / ticket_ids — the exact code path whose prior bug this change corrects (corpus 1,793 -> 1,795 by no longer dropping Jira-bridged tickets) — ships with no regression test, so the fix is not locked and a re-introduction of the same class of bug (ambiguous-prefix mis-resolution, or filtering out non-four-quad ids) would go undetected.
scenarios: A future refactor of _prefix_index re-introduces four-quad-only filtering, silently shrinking the corpus again with no failing test
An ambiguous short prefix is mis-attributed to a single ticket, skewing ticket-level correlations that back the ADR decision
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests/scripts/test_backtest_all_work.py (loaded via the existing tests/scripts/conftest.py sys.path convention) that builds a small full_ids set including a 'jira-reb-596' id and asserts a commit trailered to it is folded in, and that a 4-char ref matching two ids increments the unresolved count.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add unit tests for _diff_paths (/dev/null skip, a//b/ strip, rename both-sides) and _total_diff_lines (header lines excluded, hunk +/- lines counted).
evidence: search_files for '_diff_paths' returns only scripts/_backtest/all_work.py (and an unrelated delta_tree.py) — no tests/ coverage
scripts/_backtest/all_work.py:59-72 `_diff_paths` skips `/dev/null`, strips `a/`,`b/` prefixes
scripts/_backtest/all_work.py:75-79 `_total_diff_lines` counts +/- lines but `not line.startswith(('+++','---'))`

Named violating inputs with no test: a diff header pair `--- a/old.py` / `+++ b/new.py` (rename) must yield BOTH paths; a `+++ /dev/null` (deletion) must not add a path; a hunk body line `+++foo` must be counted by _total_diff_lines while the header `+++ b/x` must not
advisory.finding: The new diff-parsing helpers _diff_paths and _total_diff_lines have no tests, though they carry non-obvious edge behavior (skipping /dev/null, stripping a/ b/ prefixes, counting renames on both sides, and excluding +++/--- header lines from the line count) that directly feeds files_touched and total_diff_lines distributions cited in the report.
scenarios: A refactor that changes prefix handling or the header exclusion silently mis-counts files_touched, corrupting the files-vs-lines control that is the ADR's decisive evidence

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add unit tests for stats.quantile (interpolated median), _ranks (tie averaging), spearman (monotone==~1.0) and correlate (n<2 -> NaN).
evidence: No tests/ file references stats.correlate/spearman/quantile (search for 'all_work'/'_backtest' in tests returns no _backtest hits)
scripts/_backtest/stats.py:54-67 `_ranks` implements average ranks with tie sharing by hand
scripts/_backtest/stats.py:17-25 `quantile` does linear interpolation with a hand-computed index

Named violating input with no test: quantile([1,2,3,4], 0.5) must return 2.5 (interpolated median) and spearman on a perfectly monotone input must return ~1.0 while a tied input must average ranks — a regression in _ranks would silently bias every reported rho
advisory.finding: The stdlib-only statistics in stats.py (quantile, spearman via _ranks/pearson, two_sided_p, correlate) — which produce every number the ADR cites — have no tests despite hand-rolled tie-averaging and interpolation that are easy to get subtly wrong.
scenarios: A change to _ranks tie handling shifts a reported rho past the 0.42 threshold the ADR uses to justify 'advisory not blocking', with no test to catch it
advisory.suggested_fix: Add tests/scripts/test_backtest_stats.py asserting stats.quantile([1,2,3,4],0.5)==2.5, stats.spearman([1,2,3],[1,2,3]) approximately 1.0, and stats.correlate([1],[1])['rho'] is NaN.
